title: Unmanned Interceptors
statementMd:
In a future autonomous interception drill, commander Alice uses $n$ unmanned interceptors (denoted as $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n$) to surround an intruding target $B$ controlled by Bob. All units move on a two-dimensional plane. Whether the interception succeeds depends not only on the initial layout, but also on the path planning strategies of both participants.

You are given the initial coordinates $A_i(x_i, y_i)$ of the $n$ interceptors and the starting position $(x_0, y_0)$ of target $B$ on the 2D plane.

**Game Rules:**

1. **Equal speed movement**: All interceptors $A_i$ and target $B$ move at a constant speed $v$ ($v  \gt  0$) at all times. They can change direction instantly at any moment.
2. **Interception rule**: If at any moment $t \ge 0$, any interceptor $A_i$ coincides with target $B$ in position, the interception succeeds and Alice wins.
3. **Optimal play**: Alice controls all interceptors cooperatively to complete the interception, while Bob controls target $B$ to avoid being caught by any $A_i$ permanently. Both sides can track each other's positions in real time and will adopt optimal strategies.

There are $q$ independent queries. For each query, a new initial position $(x_0, y_0)$ of target $B$ is given. For every query, determine whether Alice is able to catch Bob under optimal play from both sides.

## Input

The first line contains two positive integers $n, q$ ($1 \le n,q \le 2 \times 10^5$).

The next $n$ lines each contain two integers $x_i, y_i$, representing the coordinates of $A_i$ ($-10^9 \le x_i, y_i \le 10^9$).

The next $q$ lines each contain two integers $x_0, y_0$, representing the initial position of target $B$ in the corresponding query.

## Output

Print $q$ lines in total. For each line, output either `Yes` or `No`. Print `Yes` if Alice can catch Bob, otherwise print `No`. The answer is case-insensitive.
